PullRequest.Title: Engineering - cache the Chromium build scripts so the Linux jobs don't depend on GitHub's rate limits
PullRequest.Body:
Refs microsoft/vscode-engineering#4300

The 23:00 insider official [498291](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498291) failed both Linux "Prepare deb package" steps. `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` got 429 from every GitHub source and 403 from Gitiles for the whole retry budget of `build/lib/chromiumSource.ts`. Earlier officials 498187 and 498190 needed 12 and 28 failed attempts before a download got through. So the build depends on GitHub's rate limits for two scripts that only change when the Chromium version does.

## Change

- `build/lib/chromiumSource.ts` reads Chromium build scripts from `.build/chromium-files/<version>/`, each with its SHA-256. `downloadChromiumFile` uses a cached file of the pinned version first. A missing or mismatched hash, content that fails validation, or a read error counts as a miss, and the usual download sources follow.
- `prefetchChromiumBuildFiles()` is the only writer of the cache. It fetches every missing build script with one attempt per source, and writes them all or none, since a saved cache entry can't be completed later. It never throws.
- `product-build-linux-setup.yml` and the Quality Checks job restore `.build/chromium-files` with `Cache@2` (key `"chromium-files-v5" | cgmanifest.json`), from the new step template `restore-chromium-build-files.yml`, and run the prefetch only on a miss. Every job needs a folder to save, since Cache@2 fails its post-job save on a missing path. Linux ARM64 Compile, for one, never downloads either script ([498311](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498311)). Quality Checks downloads `update.py` through `setup-env.sh`, and got the same 429s and 403 in its first round in [498329](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498329).
- Both steps use `continueOnError`, so a cache or prefetch problem falls back to today's downloads.

Cache@2 scopes entries per pipeline and branch. A cache saved by a pull request or another branch is never restored on main or a release branch, which is what guards against an untrusted writer. The hash guards against a damaged entry.

## Validation

- `build/lib/test/chromiumSource.test.ts`: 11 tests, including cache hits, other versions, invalid, unreadable and tampered entries, and the prefetch under 429s, partial failures and write failures. tsc and oxlint are clean.
- Non-publishing pipeline 111 runs on this branch (Linux x64 and arm64, `VSCODE_PUBLISH` false):
  - Miss path, [498326](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498326): both Compile jobs missed, prefetched and saved, and both Sign jobs ran "Prepare deb package" with `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` from the cache. All six Linux jobs succeeded.
  - Hit path, [498329](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498329): every Linux job restored the cache, skipped the prefetch and used both scripts from it, with no download.
  - Final head, all-or-nothing prefetch and Quality Checks, with a new key to force a miss: [498332](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=498332). Both Compile jobs and Quality Checks missed, prefetched and saved, Quality Checks used `update.py` from the cache, and both Sign jobs restored the cache, skipped the prefetch and packaged with `dpkg-shlibdeps.pl` from it. All seven jobs succeeded, and every cache and prefetch step succeeded.
- ADO previews of pipelines 111 and 727 on this branch expand the new template in every Linux job and in Quality Checks.

## Residual risk

- The first run after a Chromium update, or any `cgmanifest.json` change, still downloads, and its jobs warm the cache for the runs after it.
- If GitHub refuses the prefetch on a miss, there is nothing to save, so the post-job save logs an issue and the next run misses and tries again. The build itself behaves as it does today.

> Authored with Copilot

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: ARM64 setup excludes the x64-only script download; Compile sets VSCODE_BUILD_ONLY:true and excludes Debian packaging. The new unconditional template and synchronous prefetch/curl implementation prove the added critical-path work. Response times are unmeasured.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous curl subprocesses and HTTP requests for two unused scripts.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Per cache-missing non-consumer job: two requests if first sources succeed; four sequential requests if the first script exhausts its sources, then prefetch aborts. Each request allows 120 seconds. Jobs do not coalesce this work.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unnecessary network waits block compilation and delay dependent jobs, potentially by minutes with stalled sources.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: ARM64 Compile made zero Chromium-script requests: update.py was x64-only, and VSCODE_BUILD_ONLY:true excluded Debian preparation and its dpkg-shlibdeps.pl download.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Common Linux setup now warms both Chromium scripts synchronously on cache misses, including jobs that use neither script.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new inclusion at product-build-linux-setup.yml:154 reaches restore-chromium-build-files.yml:14 on every cache-missing ARM64 Compile job, adding synchronous downloads where that job previously made none.
Findings.Title: Skip blocking cache warm-up in jobs that consume neither script
Findings.Impact: Cold-cache ARM64 compilation and dependent signing/test jobs now wait on potentially slow Chromium sources despite needing neither downloaded script.
Findings.Evidence: product-build-linux.yml:60-66 sets VSCODE_BUILD_ONLY:true; product-build-linux-compile.yml excludes package preparation in this mode. setup-env.sh:40-45 downloads update.py only for x64. The newly included template runs prefetchChromiumBuildFiles, whose loop synchronously fetches both scripts (chromiumSource.ts:139-141). With GITHUB_TOKEN there are four sequential sources, using spawnSync curl with --max-time 120. A failing first script can consume eight minutes of configured request time before this otherwise independent compile proceeds. continueOnError does not avoid waiting.
Findings.Recommendation: Skip this restore/prefetch template for jobs consuming neither script, such as ARM64 Compile; warm the complete cache from consumer/producer jobs instead.

Scenarios.Scenario: ARM64 product Compile, followed by dependent Sign/test jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Common Linux setup completes before dependency installation and compilation; Sign and product tests depend on Compile. The added prefetch is synchronous and therefore on this path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Azure pipeline cache lookup/restore and conditional post-job upload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One restore task per job, with up to two task retries on failure; a successful cache-missing job also attempts a post-job save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restore completes before prefetch and compilation; save is after job work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: spawnSync curl to GitHub API, authenticated/anonymous raw GitHub, and Gitiles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two HTTP requests if each script's first source succeeds; four sequential requests if the first script exhausts all authenticated/fallback sources, then prefetch aborts.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Zero Chromium-script requests in ARM64 Compile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks compilation despite neither script being needed; each request permits 120 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existence checks, script/hash reads, directory creation, writes, and SHA-256 verification.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two file/hash pairs per version; cache writes occur only after all missing downloads succeed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous work before compilation; no collection-sized allocation or unbounded in-process retention.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two fixed Chromium scripts per cache-missing job, not per source file or native module. With the configured token, a failing first script attempts four sources and aborts before the second script.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One curl subprocess/request at a time inside each prefetch. Jobs have separate directories and do not coalesce requests. Dependent signing/testing cannot start until Compile finishes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cache@2 keys the directory by cgmanifest.json. An exact restored hit skips prefetch; a miss or restore failure invokes prefetch. ARM64 Compile has no actual script consumer: setup-env.sh downloads update.py only for x64, and VSCODE_BUILD_ONLY:true excludes Debian package preparation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced architecture guard, compile-only packaging exclusion, unconditional added template, synchronous prefetch, and per-request timeout.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual miss frequency and source latency are unmeasured. Eight minutes for four stalled requests is a configured upper bound, not an observed duration.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported one medium-severity eager-work regression: non-consumer jobs newly block on remote cache warming.

Scenarios.Scenario: x64 compilation, CI tests, and Quality dependency installation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Cache restoration and prefetch finish before setup-env.sh, native dependencies, compilation/tests, and Quality's subsequent work. setup-env.sh then needs update.py to initialize its compiler toolchain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Pipeline cache restore/save of the two scripts and hashes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One restore task per participating job; conditional post-job upload on a miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restore is before dependency installation; upload is after job work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On first-source success, two prefetch requests rather than the previous one update.py request per active x64 setup. Warm cache: zero script requests. Failed first-file prefetch: four requests with a token, followed by the unchanged demand retry path if needed; demand permits four rounds of four sources and 100 seconds total backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only demanded update.py was downloaded during setup, using the existing source fallbacks and retries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Successful warm hits remove remote download waits; cold prefetch of the unused packaging script can add waits before setup continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute downloaded update.py, libcxx-fetcher, and existing cached sysroot acquisition/extraction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per x64 setup invocation; downstream toolchain/sysroot acquisition depends on existing local artifacts and stamps.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same script execution, toolchain preparation, and stamp-controlled sysroot downloads occurred; the PR changes only how the two source scripts are obtained.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required existing compiler preparation still gates native dependency installation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two fixed scripts per missing cache, although these jobs normally need only update.py. product-build-ci.yml declares seven Linux test jobs, one image job, and parallel Quality; actual simultaneously running jobs depend on agent availability.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Requests and files are serialized inside a job. Eligible jobs independently prefetch on misses, with no cross-job single-flight or global limiter in the changed code. Cache saves happen after job completion and do not combine contemporaneous cold requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A complete exact hit skips prefetch and serves update.py via two file reads and hashing. On a cold successful prefetch, both scripts are saved and the immediate update.py demand uses the cache. If either download fails, fetched content is not committed; demand downloads retain the original retries. A successful update.py prefetch followed by a failed dpkg-shlibdeps.pl prefetch therefore causes update.py to be fetched again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for request counts, first-failure abort, all-or-none writes, existing retries, and independent job scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timings or agent-level concurrency measurements are available. Rate-limit prevalence is not inferred solely from the PR description.
Scenarios.Verdict: Warm-cache downloads improve. Additional unused-file prefetch is the same eager-warming root cause already reported, not a separate finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Linux Sign job prepares Debian and RPM packages
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Sign waits for Compile and CLI, runs common setup, downloads compilation artifacts, and prepares packages. Debian dependency discovery waits for sysroots and the dpkg-shlibdeps script before invoking Perl for binaries.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore/prefetch/cache-read path for update.py and dpkg-shlibdeps.pl.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pipeline-cache restore per Sign job; warm script consumers each read their script/hash pair. A cold successful prefetch makes two first-source HTTP requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: x64 setup downloaded update.py, and Debian preparation downloaded dpkg-shlibdeps.pl once per process; ARM setup did not require update.py.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restoration/prefetch gates setup and packaging; warm hits remove demand HTTP.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve sysroot metadata/assets, checksum them, and extract tarballs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Chromium sysroot metadata curl per Debian preparation; tarball download/extraction only on stamp misses. VS Code sysroot stamp misses retrieve release metadata and the selected asset, using the existing retry helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical calls, placement, retries, and stamp checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These existing sysroot dependencies complete before Debian dependency calculation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Find native modules and execute dependency scanners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One find subprocess per getDependencies invocation, then one Perl or RPM find-requires subprocess per discovered binary; script download is memoized once per process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same per-binary subprocess cardinality; the PR does not amplify it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing serial dependency scanning gates package preparation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One dpkg-shlibdeps script acquisition per Debian preparation process, not per binary, because getDpkgShlibdepsScript memoizes its destination. Perl/find-requires executions scale with native modules plus the existing executable list.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Common setup and source downloads are sequential. Debian's files.map performs synchronous per-binary Perl calls, with a single memoized script download. Separate architecture Sign jobs can run concurrently after their dependencies.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A restored complete Chromium cache eliminates source-script HTTP. Miss prefetch tries both scripts once per source; failure preserves existing on-demand download retries. The per-process dpkg script memoization remains intact. Existing sysroot stamps avoid tarball downloads, although Chromium sysroot metadata is still retrieved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced Gulp prepare-deb through getDependencies and the explicit process-level script memoization; RPM uses its own unchanged scanner.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Binary counts and existing scanner durations are unmeasured; they do not control the changed source-download cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate regression: cache hits remove remote work, and existing per-binary subprocess costs must not be attributed to this PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workspace-image producer already has a current image
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing conditions skip expensive image installation when the current image is already cached, but the new Chromium cache template is unconditional. This producer is not a dependency of test jobs, so its work is off their critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore and potentially warm Chromium scripts even when image dependency installation is skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new Chromium cache restore, plus two source requests on first-source success when that cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A current image caused the guarded dependency/sysroot installation steps to be skipped, with no Chromium-script downloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds producer job latency and agent occupation, but does not directly block test jobs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One image producer per configured Linux architecture, two fixed Chromium scripts on its independent cache miss.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous prefetch within the producer; producer and CI test jobs run independently. No cross-job request coalescing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workspace-image and Chromium-file caches have separate keys and outcomes. A workspace-image hit does not suppress the new Chromium prefetch if the Chromium cache is missing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for unconditional inclusion versus existing guarded installation and independent job dependencies.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of differing cache outcomes is unknown; producer work is explicitly off the tests' dependency path.
Scenarios.Verdict: Same non-consumer eager-warming mechanism as the submitted finding; no duplicate report.

Scenarios.Scenario: Non-pipeline download and invalid or unreadable cache fallback
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A caller synchronously obtains a demanded script before executing it or generating dependencies.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/verify cached bytes and write the requested destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded number of existence checks and up to two reads per demanded script, plus a destination write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Direct network retrieval followed by destination write.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous overhead before unchanged demand downloads or before returning a hit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Demand-driven synchronous curl downloads and retry backoff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same existing source/retry cardinality on a miss; zero HTTP on a valid hit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every demand invoked this HTTP path; the PR adds a cache bypass without increasing this demand retry loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Still blocks the demand caller only when the file is absent from the valid cache.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Only the demanded file per invocation; Debian still memoizes one acquisition per process. Cache contents are two fixed scripts per prefetched version, and CI jobs use separate workspaces.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All operations are synchronous per caller; no new background workers, retained listeners, growing in-memory cache, or cross-call queue.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ordinary downloads never populate the cache. Missing, unreadable, invalid, wrong-version, or hash-mismatched entries fall back to the original network retry behavior. A hit reads content/hash and validates SHA-256. Prefetch catches failures and writes only after all fetches succeed; write failure attempts cache cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded cache reads, unchanged miss retries, no ordinary-download cache writes, and buffer lifetime.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Local prefetch usage and file sizes were not profiled; no evidence of a hot unbounded local workload.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional high-confidence performance regression. Reduced warm-path requests are evident, but the available blame does not establish that the earlier unconditional download behavior itself introduced a historical performance regression, so no regression-fix provenance signal was submitted.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all five changed files and all diff pages, with caller, packaging, sysroot, CI-concurrency, and workspace-image analysis. Submitted one medium-severity finding for synchronous cache warming in jobs that consume neither script. Deduplicated other eager-prefetch manifestations; found no separate retention, serialization, or per-binary fan-out regression. Static analysis only.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
